newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish bonds off highs amid French vote worries.
newsitem.headline: Finnish bonds off highs amid French vote worries.

text.p: 1305/1005 GMT - Bonds off early highs in quiet trade Friday as worries mount that French socialists may win final round of parliamentary elections which could lead to a softer EMU, operators say. Bundesbank/German government gold row eyed closely. DEM/FIM in 3.0050-3.02 range, generates healthy demand.
*FIM-06 yld pct 6.27 vs 6.29 *06 gap over Bund bps 31 vs 34
*FIM-04 yld pct 5.86 vs 5.88 *FIM-99 yld pct 3.78 vs 3.79
*Jun FRAs 3.09 pct vs 3.10 *March FRAs 3.80 pct vs 3.82

Bonds slipped in early Friday afternoon trade on worries about the future of European economic and monetary union (EMU) if the French socialists win the second round of parliamentary elections on June 1, dealers said.
"There is simply no activity on the market -- investors are just sitting on their positions and waiting for the outcome of the French vote," one dealer said.
A French socialist election win had already been partly priced in the early part of the week, but operators expected yields to rise more if the socialists won the final vote.
"It will signal a wider and a softer EMU," said one.

The row between the Bundesbank and the German government which erupted on Wednesday, was also seen undermining the value of the euro currency. "The longer the matter remains unresolved the worse it is for the euro," one forex dealer said.
Markets shrugged off a 5.9 percent rise in domestic March GDP.

The markka was firmer against the mark on overseas buying which some forex dealers said was prompted by a large amount of the 2006 bond issued to overseas investors at Thursday's auction. The markka was seen in a 3.0050-3.02 range today.
